rows.why: S1 depends on how a stored value is cleaned before matching: case is ignored and the ends are trimmed. Item 2's pick lowercases and trims, so "Draft" becomes draft and " PUBLISHED " becomes published.

Item 1 asks which old spellings are read as a status. Its pick maps only "in review", so "under_review" and "LIVE" would not read as review and published, which S2 expects along with the rest of its table.

S3 says an unrecognised value reads as no status instead of the nearest match, which is what item 3 asks. Its pick returns null. Item 4 (empty or whitespace-only gives null) covers the empty-value part and agrees too, but item 3 is the closer fit.
S4 only checks that a valid enum value is stored unchanged. No item asks this. Item 5 is about near-miss input, and either answer to it would still store "review" as "review".

S5 depends on whether writing normalises near-miss input such as a different case, padding or an old spelling, which is item 5's question. Its pick accepts only exact lowercase enum strings and throws for everything else. Item 6 covers how the error names the value and is consistent with S5, but it is secondary here.

S6 mainly says how unreadable values are reported: each distinct original value once, sorted, exactly as stored. That is item 8's question. Its pick de-duplicates by exact raw value and sorts with the default sort, which matches.
